subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Cellular therapy and bispecific antibodies: CAR-T design, cytokine release syndrome, ICANS and clinical indications

steps.tx: Autologous **CAR-T cell therapy** genetically reprograms patient T lymphocytes using retroviral or lentiviral vectors to express synthetic chimeric antigen receptors. Chimeric receptors incorporate single-chain variable fragments targeting cell surface antigens such as **CD19** in B-cell malignancies or BCMA in multiple myeloma, paired with intracellular CD3-zeta and costimulatory domains 4-1BB or CD28. This synthetic architecture allows potent cytotoxic tumour lysis independently of major histocompatibility complex presentation.

steps.tx: The left cell is a reprogrammed **hunter lymphocyte** whose surface hook, the **binding arm**, grips CD19 on the tumour cell at right. Locking on fires inner **signal tails** built from costimulatory and zeta chains, waking the killer program. The hunter then dumps pore forming granules that punch holes in the target, so **tumour lysis** follows through perforin and granzyme attack without needing normal antigen presentation.
steps.say: The engineered lymphocyte carries a synthetic surface hook that grips CD19 on the malignant cell. Binding triggers internal signal tails that activate the killer program independently of normal antigen presentation. The activated cell releases pore forming proteins and enzymes that rupture the tumour membrane and complete the kill. This direct lysis design explains potent responses in B lineage cancers carrying the target.

vis.alt: An engineered lymphocyte grips its tumour target while internal signals trigger granule release that ruptures the cell.
vis.caption: Cells show surface gripping, signal firing and granule lysis of the target. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Rapid in vivo expansion of infused effector cells triggers systemic hyperinflammation termed **Cytokine release syndrome**. Activated CAR-T cells and bystander monocyte-macrophages release massive quantities of **interleukin-6**, interferon-gamma, and tumour necrosis factor-alpha. Manifestations range from high fevers and tachycardia in grade 1 disease to refractory distributive shock, capillary leak, and severe hypoxic respiratory failure requiring intensive care in grade 4 toxicity.

rows: Persistent fever without hypotension or hypoxia
Hypotension responsive to IV fluids; mild hypoxia
High-dose methylprednisolone and ICU mechanical support

steps.tx: Humanized monoclonal antibody **Tocilizumab** acts as a competitive antagonist of both soluble and membrane-bound interleukin-6 receptors. Administered intravenously, tocilizumab halts downstream inflammatory cascades, providing rapid resolution of haemodynamic instability and fever in **cytokine release syndrome**. When hypotension proves refractory to initial tocilizumab doses, guideline-directed protocols mandate immediate initiation of high-dose corticosteroids.

left.title: Tocilizumab Mechanism
points: Blocks soluble and membrane IL-6 receptors
Rapid reversal of fever and vasodilation
Does not cross the blood-brain barrier
May transiently elevate serum IL-6 levels

right.title: Corticosteroid Role
points: Essential for neurotoxicity (ICANS) and refractory CRS
May blunt long-term CAR-T expansion if prolonged

steps.tx: **Tocilizumab** is an IL-6 receptor antagonist and the first-line agent for CRS that is severe or life-threatening, given for adults and children. For severe CRS the usual dose is 8 mg/kg, and up to three further doses may be given at intervals of at least 8 hours if there is no improvement. Dexamethasone is added for steroid-refractory cases. Tocilizumab does not treat ICANS well, so neurological toxicity needs separate management.
steps.say: Tocilizumab is an interleukin 6 receptor antagonist and the first-line agent for cytokine release syndrome that is severe or life-threatening, given to adults and children. vis.alt: Diagram illustrating tocilizumab's mechanism: blocking IL-6 from binding to its receptor, thereby reducing inflammation in cytokine release syndrome.
vis.caption: Tocilizumab blocks IL-6 receptor, mitigating cytokine release syndrome

steps.tx: Immune effector cell-associated **neurotoxicity** syndrome presents with toxic encephalopathy, expressive aphasia, cognitive slowing, and tremors, progressing to status epilepticus or fatal cerebral oedema. Because tocilizumab fails to penetrate the blood-brain barrier and can transiently elevate central nervous system cytokine levels, **ICANS** management relies primarily on prompt intravenous **dexamethasone** or high-dose methylprednisolone alongside aggressive anti-epileptic prophylaxis.

steps.tx: Bispecific antibody construct **Blinatumomab** represents a **bispecific T-cell engager** BiTE comprising two flexible single-chain variable fragments. One arm binds the invariant CD3 subunit of the T-cell receptor complex, while the other engages CD19 expressed on malignant and normal B-lineage cells. Blinatumomab forms cytolytic immunological synapses, inducing targeted perforin- and granzyme-mediated lysis of minimal residual disease-positive or relapsed B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia.

left.title: Bispecific Engagers (BiTEs)
points: Directs polyclonal host T cells without ex vivo expansion

right.title: Autologous CAR-T Cells
points: Living cell therapy; expands dynamically in vivo
Requires complex patient apheresis and manufacturing
Durable multi-year persistence in bone marrow

steps.tx: Full-length IgG-like bispecific antibody **Teclistamab** simultaneously redirects CD3-positive cytotoxic T lymphocytes against the B-cell **maturation antigen** BCMA abundantly expressed on plasma cells. In the pivotal MajES-TEC-1 trial, teclistamab produced profound and durable overall response rates exceeding 60% in heavily pretreated relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Step-up subcutaneous dosing schedules mitigate cytokine release syndrome severity during treatment initiation.

steps.tx: First-in-class immune-mobilizing monoclonal TCR construct **Tebentafusp** combines an affinity-enhanced soluble T-cell receptor targeting gp100 peptide presented by HLA-A*02:01 with an anti-CD3 scFv domain. Tebentafusp achieved a landmark overall survival breakthrough in HLA-A*02:01-positive metastatic **uveal melanoma**, becoming the first approved systemic agent to prolong survival in this traditionally treatment-refractory ocular malignancy.

rows: High-affinity recognition of intracellular melanoma antigen
Invariant CD3 epsilon chain on T cells
Recruits and redirects polyclonal CD8+ and CD4+ T cells
Induces antigen-dependent targeted tumour cell cytotoxicity

steps.tx: Adoptive cellular therapy **Lifileucel** utilizes autologous **tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte** TIL cultures harvested surgically from patient melanoma metastases. Following extensive ex vivo expansion and activation with interleukin-2, TILs are re-infused following non-myeloablative lymphodepletion with cyclophosphamide and fludarabine, followed by systemic high-dose aldesleukin. Lifileucel delivers durable objective responses in patients with metastatic melanoma who have progressed through prior anti-PD-1 and targeted kinase therapies.
